_comment: Michigan 2026-2027 LIHTC Scoring Criteria, MSHDA, version 01.2026. Michigan's QAP itself does not carry point values; they live in this companion self-score workbook, which is an Excel form printed to PDF. Completion of it is mandatory. The Quick Reference Sheet on PDF p.47 names every criterion with its possible points and a section total, and the body pp.2-46 carries the detail; both were read and they agree throughout, with no contradiction of the kind Delaware has. Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed 'Page N of 48' footer. FOUR TRACKS, because Michigan's sections are not all available to the same project: Tab A Urban and Tab B Rural are mutually exclusive ('A project will only be eligible for points from the applicable Tab A or B') and each totals 44; Section E applies only to permanent supportive housing developments and totals 53; Sections C, D and F apply to everyone and total 78. An urban PSH project could therefore face 44 + 78 + 53 = 175, and an urban non-PSH project 122. The workbook states no grand total: the GRAND TOTAL cell on p.47 is part of the blank self-score column. Section D's stated total of 11 counts only its two positive criteria (7 + 4) and excludes its four negative ones (-5, -20, -20, -20), which confirms that negative points sit outside the stated maxima here as they do elsewhere in the corpus.

track_totals.note: Tab A, Urban Opportunity Criteria, 'Section Total: 44' on the Quick Reference Sheet. Mutually exclusive with the rural track. Urban areas are those ineligible as rural on the USDA RD multifamily tool.

Tab B, Rural Opportunity Criteria, 'Section Total: 44'. The seven criteria mirror the urban track name for name and point for point; only the distance thresholds differ, with rural amenities measured to 5 miles where urban are measured to 2.

Section E, Permanent Supportive Housing Developments, 'Section Total: 53'. Available only to projects meeting all of Addendum III including its threshold criteria. The workbook adds that MSHDA 'will not take into consideration any points for permanent supportive housing awarded in this Section E ... when awarding credit from the undesignated category', so these points do not travel across categories.

Not stated as a single figure by MSHDA; it is the sum of the three section totals that apply to every project, printed individually on p.47: Development Characteristics 62, Development Team Characteristics 11, Cost Reasonableness with Credit Efficiency 5. Recorded here so the base track reconciles; flagged for the reviewer as a figure computed from three stated section totals rather than read from the page.

criteria.heading: Proximity to transportation

tiers.tier_label: Public transport stop within a quarter mile, or a dial-a-ride service running at least 5 days a week
Applicant provides transport comparable to or exceeding a typical fixed route system

criteria.note: Distances measured in a straight line. Comparable transport must allow each tenant at least two trips a week, and the workbook works the sum: a 15-passenger van running two routes a day, five days a week, carries 150 passengers weekly and so covers a 75-unit development. Scattered sites are scored by unit-weighted average with no partial points, rounded down.

criteria.heading: Proximity to amenities

tiers.tier_label: Full service grocery or supermarket
Licensed childcare if undesignated, or senior center if elderly
Pharmacy
General medicine physician or clinic
Public library
Public school
Community organization
Employment center
Public park
Job training center

criteria.tier_note: The ten amenities sum to exactly 25, so this is a full tariff rather than a capped menu.
criteria.note: The single largest criterion in the urban track and, with C.2, the joint largest in the workbook. Amenities within 1 mile pay full value and those within 2 miles pay half, rounded down. The definitions are unusually specific: a full service grocery must stock nine named categories from fresh produce to personal care items; an employment center needs 250 year-round full-time employees at one location for urban developments and 125 for balance of state; little lending libraries, mobile libraries and libraries inside a school do not count; a school must be free and may not be gender-exclusive; and the same location cannot be counted as both a community organization and a job training center. MSHDA determines eligibility 'in its sole discretion'.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization plan area
criteria.note: One point, for a criterion whose documentary burden is among the heaviest in the workbook: a signed letter or resolution from the local government dated within 60 days of the application deadline that identifies the plan, links to it, outlines its goals, defines the target area boundaries and describes how the project complements it. Where no revitalization plan exists the letter must instead certify significant public and private investment nearby, on a scale stepped by municipal population: at least $5 million within 2 miles over the last 5 years for municipalities of 10,000 or fewer, at least $20 million for 10,001 to 25,000, and at least $40 million for 25,001 to 50,000, each with a forward-looking investment test as well.

criteria.heading: Household overburdened area

tiers.tier_label: 30.0% to 39.9% of households overburdened
40.0% to 49.9% of households
50.0% and above of households

criteria.detail_external: Tab HH of the MSHDA Combined Application
criteria.note: Determined by census tract, but a development within a third of a mile of a higher-scoring tract may claim that tract's score, measured from the property line to the tract boundary. The workbook gives its own worked example of a project in a 2-point tract claiming 3.

criteria.heading: Communities without recent awards
criteria.note: For developments in counties that have received no reservation of 9% credits in the last four funding rounds. A geographic-spreading device measured at county level rather than by tract or municipality.

criteria.heading: Community supported initiatives

tiers.tier_label: Place-based developer involvement
Community supported initiative without a place-based developer

criteria.note: The form instructs applicants to 'Mark an "x" in up to ONE box', which is what makes the tiers alternative rather than additive. A place-based developer is headquartered and works primarily within the local municipality, county or economic region and must hold at least 25% ownership. The supporting plan, RFP or documented outreach must have been initiated within 24 months before the deadline; HUD Choice Neighborhood areas are given as an example.

criteria.heading: Job growth opportunities

tiers.tier_label: Project located within 15 miles of the eligible site
Project located within 25 miles of the eligible site

criteria.detail_external: MSHDA list of qualifying economic development projects and priority communities, published before each round
criteria.note: Measured against new economic development projects funded with significant state resources, such as MEDC SOAR funds. Both the qualifying sites and the priority community list are published per round rather than fixed in the workbook, so the test cannot be evaluated from this document alone.

criteria.heading: Proximity to transportation
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.1, at the same value. Rural areas are those so defined by the USDA RD Multifamily map.

criteria.heading: Proximity to amenities
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.2 with the same 25-point tariff and the same amenity list, but measured over longer distances: amenities within the required rural distance pay full value and those within 5 miles pay half, against 1 and 2 miles in the urban track. Rounded down to the nearest whole point, and for scattered sites to the nearest half point.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization plan area
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.3, carrying the same population-stepped investment thresholds.

criteria.heading: Household overburdened area
criteria.detail_external: Tab HH of the MSHDA Combined Application
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.4, on the same 30/40/50 percent scale.

criteria.heading: Communities without recent awards
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.5.

criteria.heading: Community supported initiatives
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.6, with the same place-based developer distinction.

criteria.heading: Job growth opportunities
criteria.note: The rural counterpart of A.7. Cited to the Quick Reference Sheet on p.47, which lists it at 4 points under Tab B, because the body pages for the rural track end before this criterion is set out at the length its urban twin receives on p.9. A reviewer should confirm whether the rural body text for this item is present in the workbook and, if so, on which page.

criteria.heading: Affordable assisted living
criteria.note: Requires prior approval by an Affordable Assisted Living steering committee of industry members, evidenced by an approval letter filed with the application. The review packet, including a concept letter and the most recent pro forma, goes in roughly 45 days before the round deadline. A project refused approval may still apply but earns nothing here.

criteria.heading: Low-income targeting
criteria.detail_external: Unit Targeting Point Calculation Form, Exhibit 1 to the Scoring Criteria
criteria.note: Joint largest criterion in the workbook, scoring depth and breadth of targeting, with lower rents required to be spread evenly across bedroom types. The calculation itself lives in an external form, but the workbook sets hard caps on what counts: no more than 10% of units at or below 20% AMI without project-based rental assistance, no more than 25% at or below 30% AMI without PBRA, and no more than 50% of units counted toward points at all without PBRA. MSHDA's own project-based vouchers earn nothing, nor does an owner-established rental subsidy reserve. Points for subsidised units require a commitment to renew through the end of the extended use period.

criteria.heading: Historic rehabilitation projects
criteria.note: One point, requiring federal Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credits, a Part 1 Historic Application already filed with the State Historic Preservation Office, a SHPO confirmation letter, a certification that the work will conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards, and the HTC named in both the financing stack and the equity letter.

criteria.heading: Affordability commitment
criteria.note: 0.34 points for each year committed beyond the 30-year floor of a 15-year compliance period plus a 15-year extended use period, rounded down, capped at 5. The workbook states that a 45-year total commitment earns the maximum, which is consistent: 15 further years at 0.34 gives 5.1. Projects using a TIF structure are ineligible.

criteria.heading: Tenant ownership
criteria.note: For offering 100% of the tax credit units for sale to their tenants at the end of the initial 15-year compliance period. Requires a detailed ownership plan covering the right of first refusal, how it is exercised, how the sale price of each unit is set, and any continuing use or deed restrictions.

criteria.heading: On site tenant services

tiers.tier_label: Child care, educational or youth programming if undesignated, or older adult programming if elderly-restricted
Homeownership preparation classes
Financial literacy classes

criteria.note: Services must exist because of the project and fall outside typical management activity; anything already available to residents in the community earns nothing, and coordinating a service does not count as providing one. Each needs an MOU or letter of intent stating frequency, which must be at least monthly, and all services must be offered face to face. The workbook is explicit that tenants cannot be required to participate and that non-participation cannot affect their lease.

criteria.heading: Energy efficient building policy
criteria.note: Scored by transfer from the MSHDA Energy Efficient Building Certificate rather than by any test set out in the workbook, so the substance sits entirely outside this document.

criteria.heading: Evidence of proper zoning
criteria.note: Evidence that the site is already properly zoned for the intended use.

criteria.heading: Evidence of site plan approval
criteria.note: Requires a letter from the local governing body confirming that the relevant board or commission has reviewed the proposal, including the level of rehabilitation work, and that no further approvals beyond staff level are needed.

criteria.heading: Accessible units
criteria.note: All or nothing: three points for committing to build and market at least 10% of units as Accessible Type A dwelling units. Remaining units with first-floor entry or lift access must be Visitable FHA Type C or meet the building code. Units must be marketed to the local Disability Network, Area Agency on Aging, local government or other disability service provider, with records kept of outreach attempts.

criteria.heading: Accessible community space
criteria.note: One room or contiguous space usable for dining, crafts, exercise, a medical clinic, socialising, study or similar, sized by a stated ratio; hallways, offices, lobbies, bathrooms, laundry rooms and exterior areas are excluded. Shared space across phases must meet the minimum for every unit in every phase and be secured by an easement. Certified by the architect, applicant and contractor at application, and again with an as-built drawing after completion.

criteria.heading: Tax abatement
criteria.note: The abatement must be in place and effective for longer than the 15-year compliance period. Documentation differs by jurisdiction: an area-wide ordinance plus either a project-specific resolution or a letter of eligibility, or else a project-specific ordinance where no area-wide one exists. MSHDA will consider alternative structures such as tax increment financing that reduce the property tax burden for at least as long, though note that C.4 excludes TIF projects from affordability commitment points.

criteria.heading: Public housing conversions
criteria.note: The project must sit on the site of the existing public housing conversion and/or preserve at least 20% of the units being converted. RAD conversions and Section 18 are named as eligible programmes, with others considered on enquiry.

criteria.heading: Project-based tenant subsidies

tiers.tier_label: New project-based tenant subsidy contract other than MSHDA PBV, or preservation of existing project-based subsidies with a commitment to renew
A third-party organisation commits to establishing a reserve to fund rental subsidies for tenants

criteria.note: The third-party reserve route generally requires enough to fund 15 years of rent payments for the vouchered units, funded in full in advance, and its terms need not mirror a traditional project-based voucher contract so long as the impact on residents is significant. MSHDA's own project-based vouchers are excluded throughout, here and in C.2.

criteria.heading: Previous experience of general partner or member

tiers.tier_label: Tier 1: non-LIHTC affordable housing development experience
Tier 1: non-LIHTC economic development using government funding
Tier 2: 1-2 LIHTC projects
Tier 2: 3-4 LIHTC projects
Tier 2: 5 or more LIHTC projects

criteria.note: The workbook states 'These points are not cumulative', which is what makes the tiers alternative despite the two-tier presentation. A successful LIHTC project is one that completed construction and received IRS Form 8609 in the last 20 years. Owners who have never completed a LIHTC development must instead show a full team, each of whose members has prior LIHTC experience. Points for two or more general partners are not added together.

criteria.heading: Previous experience of management agent
criteria.note: Requires at least three years of LIHTC management experience and is scored on years managed, so the application must state when management of each project began. Projects carrying uncorrected Form 8823 findings outstanding longer than six months cannot be counted. Where there are several agents, points follow the one with the greatest experience and are not summed. The scoring agent, or a replacement of equivalent capacity approved by MSHDA, is expected to stay for the 15-year compliance period.

criteria.heading: Rental development's temporary point reduction
criteria.note: Assessed at MSHDA's sole discretion where the applicant or a related party failed to meet requirements on a prior project, round by round, and may apply to every project submitted across two funding rounds. Applicants are notified and given the chance to remedy before the deduction is applied. Examples include failing to follow through on representations that earned points on a funded project.

criteria.heading: Asset management's noncompliance letters policy
criteria.note: A deduction four times the size of the largest positive criterion in this section. It travels with the team: if a related entity is subject to a noncompliance letter, any project submitted with that team member takes the deduction. Where it is assessed, previous-experience points may also be withheld, decided case by case. Note that the workbook cross-refers to 'Section C.1' for those experience points where the experience criterion is in fact D.1; a reviewer should confirm.

criteria.heading: Poor previous participation of applicant
criteria.note: Covers the applicant or any related party, including failure to use a commitment or allocation of credit and failure to meet carryover allocation requirements.

criteria.heading: Poor previous participation of management agent
criteria.quote: Poor Previous Participation of Management Agent
criteria.note: Triggered by late or incorrect monitoring reports, failure to verify tenant income and rents under federal rules, outstanding HUD 2530 violations, uncorrected Form 8823 findings, or serious and repeated programme violations. Applicants are encouraged to check with MSHDA's asset management and compliance unit before the deadline to find out whether they are exposed.

criteria.heading: Supportive service coordination

tiers.tier_label: Caseworker staffing at a minimum of 1:20
Caseworker staffing at a minimum of 1:15
Caseworker staffing at a minimum of 1:12

criteria.note: Clients are counted as one per PSH unit. The workbook works the example: 35 PSH units means 35 clients, so the 1:15 ratio needs 2.333 caseworkers, rounded up to 3.

criteria.heading: Service funding commitments

tiers.tier_label: Minimum of $4,000 per PSH unit targeted for supportive services
Minimum of $6,000 per PSH unit
Minimum of $8,000 per PSH unit

criteria.note: Sources must be non-LIHTC or project cash flow, such as private or foundation funding or general partner capital contributions from developer fee. Firm commitment letters are required, the money must reach the project within the first two years of service, and in-kind commitments do not qualify.

criteria.heading: Targeted supportive housing populations

tiers.tier_label: Option 1a: at least 25% of total populations served are households meeting the HUD Category 1 or Category 4 homeless definition with a disability, or veterans with a disability rating
Option 2a: at least 25% of total project units serve the most vulnerable populations, meaning chronically homeless households or households referred from the Data Match list

criteria.note: The largest criterion in the PSH track. Scored under either Option 1 or Option 2, which are alternatives to each other; each option carries further sub-items beyond the first, so the two tiers recorded here are the ones actually read on p.39 and do not by themselves account for the stated 12. A reviewer should confirm how the remaining points are composed. Targeted units must appear in the tenant selection plan and the Continuum of Care letter of support, with a service agency commitment for that population, documented screening and prioritisation, and a preferenced waiting list. MSHDA states the intent that recovery housing developments can qualify here through a Data Match identifying drug treatment court participants with a substance use disorder who are homeless under HUD Category 1 or 4.

criteria.heading: Developing in a high need area
criteria.quote: Developing in a High Need Area
criteria.note: Awarded under one of several items based on the number of homeless persons in the project's county, evidenced by the county's most recent annual literally homeless (Category 1) count. The individual tier values were not read and are not recorded here; only the stated maximum of 5, which appears both on p.40 and on the Quick Reference Sheet.

criteria.heading: Experienced supportive housing development team

tiers.tier_label: General partner or member owns and operates 50 or more units of supportive housing
Management agent has experience managing 50 or more units of supportive housing
Lead agency has experience providing services for 50 or more units of permanent supportive housing

criteria.note: Three independent roles at three points each, summing exactly to the stated 9, so this is additive rather than a ladder. Experience may come from LIHTC PSH units or HUD-funded PSH such as HUD 811 or Continuum of Care programmes. Senior developments do not count.

criteria.heading: On site PSH services
criteria.note: The PSH counterpart of C.6, for services accessible to all within the community and provided in conjunction with the development. Individual service values were not read; the stated maximum of 3 appears on p.41 and on the Quick Reference Sheet.

criteria.heading: Medicaid experience
criteria.note: For a service team member who currently bills Medicaid, or contracts with a Medicaid billing agency, in a permanent supportive housing, behavioural health or substance use disorder setting. Distinct from E.8, which rewards a forward commitment rather than existing practice, so a project can hold both.

criteria.heading: Medicaid billing
criteria.note: For the lead agency committing to bill Medicaid or contract with a Medicaid billing agency in the same settings, highlighted in the Addendum III application form.

criteria.heading: Coordinated entry system

tiers.tier_label: Coordinated Entry is the only referral source for all PSH units
Coordinated Entry is the only referral source for units serving HUD Category 1, Category 4 and chronically homeless populations

criteria.note: Must be documented in the MOU. The full four points require exclusivity across every PSH unit, not only the units serving the priority categories.

criteria.heading: Recovery housing developments
criteria.note: Requires prior review and approval by a Recovery Housing steering committee drawn from the Michigan Association of Treatment Court Professionals, evidenced by an approval letter filed with the application. Structured like C.1: without the committee's approval the points are simply unavailable.

criteria.heading: Cost reasonableness with credit efficiency
criteria.note: Mandatory for all projects and the only bidirectional criterion in the workbook: eligible credit per LIHTC unit is compared with a safe harbour set 2.5% above and below a five-year average for that building type, inflated for yearly cost increases. Inside the band is 0 points, below it earns up to 5, above it costs up to 5 negative. Recorded at its positive maximum of 5, which is the figure the Quick Reference Sheet carries; the symmetric downside is not separately recorded as a negative criterion because it is the same test. Unit counts are weighted by bedroom size before the comparison, at 0.90 for studios, 1.00 for one-bedroom, 1.15 for two-bedroom and 1.25 for three or more, and new construction, preservation, and vacant uninhabitable rehabilitation or adaptive reuse are each measured against their own average.
